A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study and contain complete main text and Appendices A–G. Their equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison despite changes in placement and numbering.

before.justification: v3 reports original annotation, retrieval and RAG experiments, including component comparisons and the NQ annotation experiment in Appendix C.

after.justification: v5 retains these original empirical results in the main text and appendices, including the NQ experiment in Appendix C.

M1.justification: The RelSel/UtilSel/UtilRank pipeline, SumMargLH objective and curriculum-learning procedure are unchanged. Appendix C adds a brief explanation of First1LH, without changing the already-described first-positive training procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions retain MS MARCO training and retrieval evaluation, 14 BEIR datasets, RAG evaluation on MS MARCO QA/NQ/HotpotQA, and NQ-specific annotation and training in Appendix C.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain Human, REPLUG and their curriculum-learning comparisons. BM25 in Table 3 and Human (First1LH) in Appendix C are also retained; no comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: The dataset splits, 200-query Hybrid Test, model configurations, two-epoch training plus one-epoch curriculum stage, top-1/top-5 RAG inputs and evaluation metrics remain unchanged in Section 4 and Appendix D.

E4.justification: Section 6 and Appendices B and E retain the same component and loss comparisons, human-label ratio and threshold sensitivities, positive inclusion/sampling experiments, and RAG top-k analysis. No analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both retain the single-run/default-seed disclosure in Appendix D.2, two-sided paired t-tests at p < 0.05, and the exclusion of corpus-level BLEU from significance testing. No uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Matched results are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 2 retains RetroMAE MRR@10 values of 38.6 for Human, 35.3 for UtilSel and 35.7 for UtilRank. The NQ results move from v3 Table 10 to v5 Table 9 without score changes.

T1.justification: Equations 1–6 retain the same likelihood objectives, dense-retrieval scoring and KL-divergence formulation. No mathematical assumption, derivation or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the claims about utility-focused annotation, improved out-of-domain retrieval/RAG, and performance comparable to full human annotation when using only 20% of human labels.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning noisy positives, in-domain versus out-of-domain generalization, and differences from original REPLUG remain unchanged. Section 8 retains the same limitations and discussion of the existing NQ experiment.

D1.justification: The implementation settings, hardware, annotation time/cost information, prompts in Appendix G, and code/data access statements are retained. The First1LH gloss supplies no distinct implementation setting beyond the earlier description.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning relative to relevance annotation, utility judgments, REPLUG and earlier retrievers are unchanged. Reference differences concern typography and reflow.

P1.justification: v5 rephrases the human-annotation-ratio sentence in Section 6, adds the First1LH gloss in Appendix C, updates author contribution symbols and revises funding acknowledgements. The section and appendix organization remains intact.

P2.justification: The same 17 tables and seven figures remain, with limited relocation and page reflow. Figure 1 moves from PDF page 4 to page 3; v3 Tables 9, 10 and 11 become v5 Tables 11, 9 and 10 respectively. Figure content and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: v5 preserves the scientific methods, empirical evidence, reproducibility information and limitations, including all appendix analyses. The First1LH clarification, small wording edits and rearranged displays are editorial refinements that leave overall paper quality essentially unchanged.
